facts.statement: The genus Murrindalaspis was described by Long in 1984.
Murrindalaspis lived during the Early Devonian period.
Murrindalaspis wallacei is the type species of the genus Murrindalaspis.
There are two known species in the genus: Murrindalaspis wallacei and Murrindalaspis bairdi.
Fossils of Murrindalaspis have been found in the McLarty Member of the Murrindal Limestone in eastern Victoria, Australia.
facts.quote: found in the McLarty Member of the Murrindal Limestone, of the Early Devonian-aged Buchan Group in eastern Victoria, Australia

facts.statement: Murrindalaspis is distinguished by a dorsal plate featuring a large, blade-like, flattened, and recurved crest originating from the medial line.
facts.quote: having a dorsal plate with a large, blade-like flattened, recurved crest emanating from the medial line

facts.statement: Unlike other acanthothoracids, Murrindalaspis lacks a ventral keel.
The type species, Murrindalaspis wallacei, possesses a high dorsal medial crest.
facts.quote: M. wallacei, the type species, has a high dorsal medial crest

facts.statement: Murrindalaspis lived between 410.62 and 393.47 million years ago during the Emsian stage.
facts.quote: Time range: Emsian to Emsian (410.62 to 393.47 million years ago)

facts.statement: Murrindalaspis belongs to the parent group Acanthothoraci.
Murrindalaspis is classified within the class Placodermi.
